slides.say: Combine a reducer with context, and any component can read and update state from far above.
Step one: create two contexts. One for the tasks, one for the dispatch function.

slides.code:
const [tasks, dispatch] =
  useReducer(tasksReducer, initialTasks);

<TasksContext value={tasks}>
  <TasksDispatchContext value={dispatch}>
    ...
  </TasksDispatchContext>
</TasksContext>
slides.say: Step two: the top component puts tasks and dispatch into those contexts.
Step three: any component below reads what it needs. No props or handlers passed down, yet the state still lives at the top.

slides.text: Bonus: wrap it in a TasksProvider with custom Hooks like useTasks().
slides.say: You can even move it all into one file, with a Tasks Provider component and custom Hooks like use tasks.
